text:
Jack Eichel is doing what a No. 1 center on a contender is supposed to do: 26 points in 21 games, 11 of them on the power play, and a Vegas team that controls 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he's out there. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.5 wins last season, sixth among all forwards, and nothing this fall says he has slipped.

The part to keep an eye on is the finishing. He has nine goals on 6.3 expected and is shooting 16%, against 10% last season, and the Golden Knights have scored almost 12 more goals than expected with him on the ice. That kind of luck tends to fade. The quieter last ten (eight points against 11.9 expected) may already be the correction starting.

What won't fade is the way he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 98th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, and he carries the puck in on 58% of his entries. With Mitch Marner now feeding him one-timers on the power play, the setup is the story, not the shooting percentage.
